reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer support for the contribution is retained because final paper P:S-6611796d53490352e9c9 documents C5-C14 enrichment cultures at 70 °C, and P:S-9bf6b9e56f066f03c6f5 identifies the two Alkanophaga taxa and their association with the sulfate-reducing partner.

The reviewer’s prior-art limit remains relevant in qualified form: final paper P:S-a21af4a61c24da8ec207 explicitly characterizes the evolutionary ordering as support for a previously established hypothesis while retaining a proposed ancestral-state interpretation.
The reviewer-described cultivation and physiological contribution is supported by final paper P:S-6611796d53490352e9c9 and P:S-9bf6b9e56f066f03c6f5.
The reviewer’s account of converging genomic, metabolite, microscopy, and transcriptomic evidence is supported by final paper P:S-9bf6b9e56f066f03c6f5 and P:S-4c6fc936cb55940f33fc.
The reported contrast in substrate range and activation position is retained because final paper P:S-20cd9a77bcad0f83ecb4 and P:S-b107c34aed1ea93c4bc2 document both observations.

The residual uncertainty over electron transfer is independently stated in final paper P:S-ea94ea798edf3959fc6e and P:S-ba03208aedb56a00301e: DIET is predicted, filament identity requires further analysis, and a soluble contribution remains possible.
Final paper P:S-b107c34aed1ea93c4bc2 identifies the alkyl-CoM-to-acyl-CoA conversion as requiring further investigation, and P:S-d5531783a42fa640159f states that propionyl-CoA fate remains unclear.

Final paper P:S-46de909925dd6dc99876 states that available sequences originate from Guaymas Basin, while P:S-c8816be41e0a82ca4311 treats occurrence in other heated petroleum-rich environments as a future possibility.
The final paper retains the Borg/MHC explanation as a possibility and states that Borg presence in other Syntrophoarchaeia remains to be examined (P:S-46de909925dd6dc99876).

The final paper assigns the dominant C14 products only to the ≥3-alkyl-CoM class in P:S-20cd9a77bcad0f83ecb4 and reports multiple activation-position peaks in P:S-a0d6fe048880bd840151; the exact identities beyond the available standards remain unresolved.
Audit-only resolved issue: final paper P:S-9bf6b9e56f066f03c6f5 uses the Alkanophaga-specific Aph183 probe, and P:S-9508ba594ede89b6b83f documents its design.
Audit-only resolved issue: final paper P:S-021d184fd5ffaadf86b3 describes the manual binning criteria and quality control.
Audit-only resolved issue: the corrected final interpretation reports only small fractions of the hydrogen expected if it were the sole carrier in P:S-ea94ea798edf3959fc6e.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Describe the evolutionary-order conclusion as support for an existing hypothesis and distinguish it from the new cultivation evidence.
limiting_points.text: The evolutionary interpretation is a qualified extension of prior work rather than a wholly new hypothesis: the final paper itself states that its phylogenetic and metabolic observations support a previously established multicarbon-before-methanotrophy hypothesis.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Retain the distinction between the new mid-chain enrichment cultures and previously characterized short- and long-chain alkane oxidizers.
supporting_points.text: The study extends archaeal alkane-oxidation physiology by linking thermophilic C5-C14 enrichment cultures to two Candidatus Alkanophaga taxa and a sulfate-reducing partner.

questions.suggested_action: Resolve the identities and relative contributions of the individual >2-C14-CoM isomers.
questions.text: Which specific >2-C14-CoM isomers account for the dominant subterminal activation signal in the C14 culture?

strengths.suggested_action: Preserve the direct linkage between enrichment activity, taxa, and syntrophic partner.
strengths.text: The work combines sustained thermophilic alkane-degrading enrichments with taxonomic identification of two Alkanophaga populations and their co-occurring sulfate-reducing partner.

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the integrated presentation of genomic, expression, inhibitor, metabolite, and microscopy evidence.
strengths.text: Multiple evidence streams support Acr-mediated alkane activation: Acr gene content and expression, BES sensitivity, alkyl-CoM detection, and targeted visualization of mixed aggregates.

strengths.suggested_action: Maintain the observed substrate-range and activation-position contrasts as separate findings.
strengths.text: The results reveal both species-associated substrate preferences and a chain-length-dependent shift from terminal to more subterminal alkane activation.

summary.text: This study establishes thermophilic enrichment cultures that oxidize petroleum n-alkanes from C5 to C14 and associates the activity with Candidatus Alkanophaga archaea, Acr-dependent alkyl-CoM formation, and a sulfate-reducing syntrophic partner. The convergent cultivation, genomic, transcriptomic, metabolite, and imaging evidence supports that contribution. The central mechanistic and ecological interpretations remain appropriately limited by unresolved electron-transfer architecture, metabolic gaps after alkyl-CoM formation, and restricted environmental occurrence data; the evolutionary conclusion is framed as support for prior work.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Differentiate direct electron transfer from possible soluble-carrier contributions and identify the intercellular conductive structures.
weaknesses.text: The electron-transfer mechanism remains inferential. The paper predicts predominantly DIET, but the observed filaments are not identified and a contribution from soluble intermediates remains possible.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Identify the alkyl-CoM-to-acyl-CoA conversion route and account for propionyl-CoA processing during odd-chain alkane oxidation.
weaknesses.text: Key steps in complete alkane oxidation are unresolved: the conversion of alkyl-CoM to acyl-CoA is unknown, and the fate of propionyl-CoA in odd-chain alkane metabolism remains unclear.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Constrain ecological statements to the sampled setting until occurrence and activity are documented in additional petroleum-rich environments.
weaknesses.text: The ecological reach of Candidatus Alkanophaga remains uncertain because currently available sequences originate from Guaymas Basin and occurrence elsewhere is presented as a future possibility.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Separate the observed absence of archaeal MHCs from the untested Borg-loss explanation.
weaknesses.text: The proposed loss of a Borg carrying multihaem cytochromes is speculative; the paper states that Borg occurrence in other Syntrophoarchaeia remains unexamined.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: A clade-specific Alkanophaga probe replaces the former general archaeal-probe basis for cell assignment.
The final methods specify the manual-binning criteria and quality-control procedure.
The corrected final treatment uses the small measured hydrogen fraction in the electron-transfer interpretation.
